title: Mondays and Thursdays
hook: the Prophet ﷺ fasted Mondays and Thursdays (Tirmidhi)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the soul of the fast: a shield. No shouting, no quarrels, and when provoked, I am fasting.

Ramadan comes once a year. But in some Muslim homes there's a quieter rhythm: an alarm set before dawn on a Sunday night, a glass of water and some dates, and then a regular Monday at work, fasting, without anyone at the next desk knowing. Then the same again on Wednesday night, for Thursday. No holiday. No crowd at iftar. Just a habit with roots in the week of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
screen: `AN ALARM ON A SUNDAY NIGHT.` → `A REGULAR MONDAY, FASTING.` → `NO CROWD, NO HOLIDAY.`

segments.voice: First, the practice itself. Reports in the collections describe the Prophet ﷺ making a point of fasting on Mondays and Thursdays. These are voluntary fasts, sunnah, not required. Much of what shapes the Ramadan fast still shapes them: dawn to sunset, food, drink and intimacy set aside, the shield on the tongue. But nobody owes them. Second, why those two days. In a report in Jami' at-Tirmidhi, the Prophet ﷺ says deeds are presented on Monday and Thursday, and he loved that his deeds be presented while he was fasting: an accounting, twice a week, and wanting to be found in the middle of a good act when it comes. Third, Monday has its own reason. In Sahih Muslim he is asked about fasting on Monday, and he answers: that is the day I was born, and the day revelation came to me. So the Monday fast is also a kind of remembering, a small anniversary kept every week. Fourth, the rhythm. A yearly fast is a mountain; a weekly one is a path you walk often. Some teachers describe voluntary fasts as a way to keep what Ramadan builds from fading over the year. And yesterday's shield goes with it: a regular Monday where the tongue is guarded and nobody else even knows. Big seasons matter. A weekly fast is something else: small, chosen, and repeated.
screen: `A VOLUNTARY FAST, TWICE A WEEK.` · `DEEDS PRESENTED, WHILE FASTING.` · `MONDAY: BORN, AND REVELATION.` · `A PATH, NOT A MOUNTAIN.`

segments.voice: Look ahead to the next Monday or Thursday. If you fast, and it's safe for your health, see yourself setting the alarm the night before, eating before dawn, and going through that ordinary day fasting. If you don't, choose one small thing to set aside that day from dawn to sunset as a way of marking it, a snack, your phone at lunch, a complaint, and if you pray, make it an intention.
Mondays and Thursdays. The voluntary weekly fasts the Prophet ﷺ kept: the days deeds are presented, and Monday, the day of his birth and of revelation. Today's word.
Your line: two days a week. Monday also remembers a birth and a revelation. Day one thousand one hundred eleven.

howItsDone: Some Muslims keep voluntary fasts on Mondays and Thursdays through the year, following the Prophet's practice, eating before dawn and breaking the fast at sunset as in Ramadan.
